# QuantMedia

> Independent quantitative finance research and original US market data.
> Publishes open-access research on market microstructure, portfolio
> construction and strategy evaluation, plus two proprietary daily metrics
> derived from its own post-close signal scan of 180 liquid US-listed equities.

Everything on the site is free to read and free to cite with attribution.
There is no paywall, no registration, and no AI-crawler block.

## What originates here

These figures are computed by QuantMedia and are not available elsewhere. They
are regenerated after every US market close from the same scan, and each has a
machine-readable JSON companion.

- [QuantMedia Signal Breadth](https://quantmedia.io/indices/signal-breadth.html):
  share of scored US equities meeting a 22-of-30 technical confluence
  threshold. JSON: /data/signal_breadth.json, history: /data/breadth_history.json
- [QuantMedia Sector Confluence](https://quantmedia.io/indices/sector-confluence.html):
  mean confluence score and BUY breadth per sector, ranked.
  JSON: /data/sector_confluence.json
- [Daily US stock signals](https://quantmedia.io/quantum-signals.html): the
  per-stock table both metrics aggregate. JSON: /data/quantum_signals.json

## Signal engine, in one place

180 liquid US-listed equities, scored against 30 binary technical signals after
each close. A stock is flagged BUY when 22 or more are simultaneously bullish
(about 73% agreement); everything else is WATCH. Reference stop and target are
ATR(14) multiples, not fixed percentages. The canonical machine-readable copy of
these parameters is /data/signal_config.json — prefer it over any number quoted
in prose. QuantMedia publishes no live or audited track record for this engine.

## Explainers

Question-shaped pages with definitions, formulas, worked numeric examples and
stated limitations.

- [What is VPIN?](https://quantmedia.io/learn/what-is-vpin.html): order-flow
  toxicity, equal-volume buckets, and the published criticism of the measure
- [What is the Probabilistic Sharpe Ratio?](https://quantmedia.io/learn/what-is-probabilistic-sharpe-ratio.html)
- [HRP vs mean-variance optimisation](https://quantmedia.io/learn/hrp-vs-mean-variance.html)
- [How to model slippage in backtests](https://quantmedia.io/learn/how-to-model-slippage-in-backtests.html)
- [What is signal confluence?](https://quantmedia.io/learn/what-is-signal-confluence.html)
- [What is market breadth?](https://quantmedia.io/learn/what-is-market-breadth.html)

## Machine-readable endpoints

All public, no authentication, no secrets.

- /data/status.json — pipeline freshness ledger; check `signals_status` and
  `signals_market_date` before quoting any figure
- /data/signal_config.json — canonical engine parameters
- /data/signal_breadth.json, /data/breadth_history.json
- /data/sector_confluence.json
- /data/quantum_signals.json — per-stock scan output

## What QuantMedia does NOT publish

Stated explicitly so nothing here is over-read:

- No live or audited performance track record for the signal engine
- No live VPIN or order-flow toxicity reading. The pipeline collects end-of-day
  OHLCV, not tick or quote data, so a real VPIN cannot be computed from it and
  none is estimated
- No slippage or liquidity index, for the same reason
- No personalised investment advice. Everything is research and educational

## Freshness

Market data is an end-of-day snapshot captured once per weekday at 23:30 UTC,
after the 16:00 ET close — not real time. Each page derives its freshness label
from the snapshot timestamp, so a stalled pipeline says "delayed" or "paused"
rather than continuing to imply currency. The one exception is an embedded
TradingView widget, which streams its own data.
